predecessors.note: The Askia court sat in Dendi from the fall of Gao in 1591 (Songhai dossier); the Dendi page: "Some members of the Askia dynasty and their followers fled here after being defeated by the invading Saadi dynasty" and set up a new capital at Lulami; this dossier starts when the Songhai dossier ends (1599).

capitals.note: "They set up a new capital at Lulami, which Askia Nuh later used too"; the page gives no coordinates (the Gaya place is a proxy).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Dendi row; its Songhai shape ends 1608). Dendi is "the easternmost province" of Songhai; the page gives no area or extent beyond its modern centres. The same outline as the Songhai dossier's 1599 successor land.

ledger.note: 1599: the Askia kingdom of Dendi on the Niger. After Tondibi the Askia fled to Dendi and set up a capital at Lulami; Askia Nuh resisted the Saadi pasha Mahmud ibn Zarqun in a two-year war ("In 1594 Mahmud was forced to discontinue the war and retreated") and "was deposed in 1599 in favor of his brother Harun". The Songhai Empire ends in 1599 in the Songhai dossier.

ledger.note: 1901: the French take Dendi. "In 1901, the French deposed the last askia of Dendi, ending Songhai's control of either Mali or Niger until independence."

ledger.note: 1901: Dendi ends. It was "conquered by France and incorporated into French West Africa"; the last askia was Malla (1887-1901).

wars.name: Dendi war against the Saadi pasha
wars.outcome: Nuh resisted the Moroccan-backed pasha Mahmud ibn Zarqun in a two-year war; "In 1594 Mahmud was forced to discontinue the war and retreated".
wars.note: No border change; the page does not mention Kebbi, Borgu, Sokoto, Gurma or the Mossi.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier, only Dendi's modern centres on the Niger.

sources.title: Dendi Kingdom
sources.note: Askia refuge at Lulami, Nuh and Mahmud ibn Zarqun 1594, rulers, French deposition 1901; no area.

notes:
Dendi Kingdom (Askia line at Lulami), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Dendi Kingdom (1 page).

Starts in 1599 to meet the songhai-empire dossier, which ends the empire in 1599 with dendi-kingdom as successor and keeps the Askia court at Lulami from 1591; the Dendi page itself dates only Nuh's war (to 1594), his deposition in 1599 and the French deposition of 1901. The ruler list on the page is partial (Hanga 1700-1761, Samsu Beri 1761-1779, Tomo 1805-1823, Dauda 1882-1887, Malla 1887-1901): no strip. Not on the page: any border, relations with Kebbi, Borgu, Sokoto, Gurma or the Mossi. Gazetteer: Lulami (place).
